sceneFacts.shortVersion: Tre's house is a real home on Cimarron Street, built in 1923.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Tre's house is a real home on Cimarron Street, built in 1923. It has also appeared in other films like 'Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood'.

sceneAnchor.anchorElement: The iconic houses of Tre, Ricky, and Doughboy in "Boyz N the Hood" were actual residences on Cimarron Street, built in 1923, and have since appeared in other films like "Don't Be a Menace to South Central While Drinking Your Juice in the Hood".

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Filming in South Central LA was a first for Hollywood.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Filming in South Central LA was a first for Hollywood. Director John Singleton insisted on telling his own story from the neighborhood.

[scene 196] 01:05:15–01:05:37
summary: The clip shows a group of African American men discussing racial stereotypes and social issues related to drug trafficking, set in an outdoor urban neighborhood environment with a serious and contemplative mood.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Ice Cube's role as Doughboy was written just for him.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Ice Cube's role as Doughboy was written just for him. He channeled personal grief for emotional scenes, as this was his acting debut.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Doughboy's crew was based on a real L.A. street gang.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Doughboy's crew was based on a real L.A. street gang. The rival Crenshaw Mafia Bloods reportedly took issue with their depiction.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 262] 01:29:22–01:30:19
summary: The clip shows a tense and sorrowful moment where a group of men are attending to a bloodied and possibly deceased individual in an urban alley, with a car parked nearby and a somber, anxious atmosphere.
cast on screen: Cuba Gooding Jr., Morris Chestnut, Ice Cube
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: A Bloods gang leader reportedly met with "Boyz N the Hood" producers to discuss a scene where Ice Cube's character was to shoot Bloods members, as it was planned near known gang territory.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Furious and Tre had a surprisingly small age gap.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Furious and Tre had a surprisingly small age gap. Laurence Fishburne, who played Furious, was only about seven years older than Cuba Gooding Jr.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 270] 01:32:34–01:32:54
summary: The clip shows a tense and emotional scene where a young man with a bloodstained shirt is confronted by others about a shooting incident involving someone named Rick, set in a neighborhood environment with distressed individuals reacting to the violence.
cast on screen: Laurence Fishburne, Cuba Gooding Jr.
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: There were surprisingly small age gaps between actors playing family members in "Boyz N the Hood"; Laurence Fishburne (father) was only seven years older than Cuba Gooding Jr. (son), and Tyra Ferrell (mother) was only seven years older than Morris Chestnut and Ice Cube (her sons).

sceneFacts.shortVersion: The director kept gunshots a secret for realistic reactions.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The director kept gunshots a secret for realistic reactions. One actor nearly got run over during a take.

sceneAnchor.sceneDescription:
[scene 295] 01:40:19–01:40:33
summary: The clip shows a tense and violent nighttime confrontation involving aggressive dialogue, a man firing a gun, and characters urgently trying to escape in a car, creating a mood of fear and conflict.
sceneAnchor.anchorElement: To achieve more realistic reactions from the cast during intense scenes, director John Singleton intentionally kept the timing of gunshots a secret from the actors in "Boyz N the Hood".

sceneFacts.shortVersion: The actor playing Chris was paralyzed in real life.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The actor playing Chris was paralyzed in real life. Redge Green's paralysis was due to a gunshot he experienced years before the film was released.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: That dead body scene? It was filmed near the Rodney King beating site.
sceneFacts.longDescription: That dead body scene? It was filmed near the Rodney King beating site. The location was just one mile from Florence and Normandie, where the beating occurred a year after the film's release.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: John Singleton was the youngest and first Black Best Director Oscar nominee.
sceneFacts.longDescription: John Singleton was the youngest and first Black Best Director Oscar nominee. He was 24 years old at the time, a record still unbroken today.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Laurence Fishburne got the script from Singleton on Pee-Wee's Playhouse.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Laurence Fishburne got the script from Singleton on Pee-Wee's Playhouse. Singleton was working as a security guard when he gave Fishburne the script for his opinion.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Ice Cube bombed his first audition for Doughboy.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Ice Cube bombed his first audition for Doughboy. He hadn't read the script, but director John Singleton gave him a second chance.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Hear those choppers? Singleton implied them to save money.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Hear those choppers? Singleton implied them to save money. He pitched the idea to the studio chief as a way to keep the budget modest.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: John Singleton wrote this film's script as his USC senior thesis.
sceneFacts.longDescription: John Singleton wrote this film's script as his USC senior thesis. Columbia Pictures quickly bought it, and he insisted on directing.
